name: TDC ADMET Solubility_AqSolDB
description: Predict the solubility of a compound in water (logarithm of the solubility in mol/L) from its molecular structure, given as a SMILES string (endpoint Solubility_AqSolDB of the Therapeutics Data Commons ADMET benchmark group). The measured compounds are split by molecular scaffold into a training, a validation and a test part. The test part is fixed; the candidate is run five times (seeds 1 to 5), each time with a different division of the other compounds into training and validation. It receives the training and validation compounds with their values and the test compounds without, and returns one prediction per test compound. Each of the five runs is a separate process that receives only these arguments: it cannot read the evaluator's files, start other processes or open network connections, and it has 700 seconds. The score is the mean absolute error on the test compounds, averaged over the five runs; lower is better.
contract: fit_predict(train_smiles, train_y, valid_smiles, valid_y, test_smiles, info) -> sequence of finite numbers, one per test molecule in the given order: the predicted value. train_smiles, valid_smiles and test_smiles are lists of SMILES strings, train_y and valid_y lists of numbers; info has name, metric, kind ('regression' or 'binary') and seed. Score: mean over the seeds 1 to 5 of the mean absolute error on the test part, minimized.
notes: Downloaded by PyTDC at first use into data/admet
Predicts the log10 aqueous solubility (mol/L) of 9,982 curated compounds from their SMILES strings, scored by mean absolute error.
Leaders are large tuned ensembles or foundation-model fine-tunes.
Needs PyTDC and rdkit: not in .venv-tasks, so the evaluator restarts itself under tools/venv-admet (created by the README's setup steps).

Every scoring call of the candidate runs in the main suite's sandbox (a child process with an audit hook, 700 s and 6 GB for one call): it keeps a search from coming across the test labels and is not a security boundary against a candidate written to attack the evaluator.
One evaluation of the starting program took 1500 s in the run of 2026-11-11, more than the arena's default limit of 120 s: raise AR_EVAL_TIMEOUT for this task.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the logarithm of the aqueous solubility (mol/L) of an organic compound from its structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Poor aqueous solubility limits absorption and complicates formulation and assays, so predicting it from structure guides compound design and chemical risk assessment.

papers.title: AqSolDB, a curated reference set of aqueous solubility and 2D descriptors for a diverse set of compounds
papers.task_relation: The task predicts the logS values of this curated set; the paper's purpose is the data set itself, so it is a data source more than a modelling paper.
papers.primary_goal: Curate a reference set of experimental aqueous solubilities of about 10,000 compounds, merged from nine datasets, for building solubility predictors.

papers.task_relation: The task predicts aqueous solubility from structure like this paper, but on the larger AqSolDB set and with an unrestricted model.
